summary: Multiple observations of the atmospheric reentry of an aerospace debris: piece of nozzle of the Soyuz launcher (which launched the COSMOS 1984 satellite) recovered in a field near Bourges (Fr).
description: On December 21, 1988, at approximately 12:50 a.m., numerous witnesses spread across France along a north-south axis observed a very bright white object with a yellow-orange trail crossing the sky. The phenomenon was extremely fast, and no sound was heard. At the end of its trajectory, the object broke into several pieces. The following day, south of Bourges, a farmer found a piece of television approximately 70 cm long in his field (see report Ne1189). After examination of the recovered piece, it was determined to be a fragment of the nozzle of the Russian Soyuz rocket (see reconstruction in the "Elements of the Investigation" documents). This rocket had launched on December 16, 1988 from Plesetsk (USSR), the COSMOS 1984 satellite (Yantar 4K2 type optical reconnaissance satellite, fell back to Earth on February 13, 1989).

summary: Observations by motorists of a luminous phenomenon seemingly blocking the road: mistaking the Moon for a moon.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. Its publications include older cases, classified at the time, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience acquired over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even an explicit change in classification within an investigation report. This particular case is among those classified as D in 1988 by SEPRA and was previously named LE VIGAN (30). On the night of December 17-18, 1988, at approximately 2:45 a.m., four witnesses traveling on the D113 in two vehicles observed a luminous object in the form of a double rectangle separated by a black line, which appeared to be blocking the road. This object is located 7 to 8 meters above the ground, directly in front of the road, and moves backward as cars advance. The phenomenon is silent. This case is consistent (three witnesses), and the description of the observed UFO is precise. The sincerity and credibility of the witnesses have never been questioned. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (shape, size, color) with a well-known astronomical object: the Moon at sunset. Furthermore, the Moon was indeed present in the area of the sky observed, even though the witnesses did not mention it. It is not the visual perception of the witnesses that is at issue, but rather their interpretation of their observation based on their feelings (astonishment, fatigue, fear, night driving). In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of moderate strangeness is classified as UFO A, an observation linked to a misidentification of the Moon.

summary: Observation by a single witness of a round, silent object stabilized above a field with several lights
description: On December 16, 1988, in the Cambrai region, at sunset, a student driving her car observed a round, silent object hovering approximately 20 meters above a field. It had four or six large lights on its underside. Additionally, light appeared in a nearby house, which was presumably abandoned. The observation lasted about a minute, as the witness did not dare stop. After investigation, the light in the house was explained by the fact that the farm was actually being used by the military for maneuvers. However, no further information could be gathered regarding the observed object, which remained unidentified.

summary: Observation of a very bright light and a dark mass: lack of information.
description: Recent report (August 5, 2013) of an earlier sighting on a Sunday in December 1988 (the exact date is not specified by the witness, and we date the event to the first Sunday of the month). One Sunday morning in December 1988, around 12:35 a.m., a driver and his passenger suddenly noticed an intense light illuminating the entire landscape. The witness turned off his headlights and observed a dark mass from which the light was coming and heard a faint buzzing sound. The light gradually disappeared, then rapidly moved westward, the landscape plunging back into darkness. This sighting mentions an imprecise date, and the account is not very detailed. The witness was very moved by the sighting, as was his wife, and the witness states that she does not wish to discuss it. No further reports were collected. The observed phenomenon (bright illumination of the sky for a few minutes) could be a luminous phenomenon behind the clouds (e.g., atmospheric re-entry of satellite debris) or glare due to fatigue. The lack of precise date information makes any verification impossible. This moderately strange and rather inconsistent case is classified as "C" due to a lack of precise information.

summary: Observation of the rapid movement of a luminous ball with electrical effects on the witness: observation of an electrical and plasma phenomenon.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even an explicit change in classification within an investigation report. This case, previously classified as D and named VERGT (24) 1988, is one of a group of cases recently re-examined. On December 1, 1988, at approximately 8:20 a.m., a witness, accompanied by his dog, was walking on the road near his home. He saw, at a distance of 60 meters, an intense light brighter than that of an arc welder. The witness described a round, blue-violet shape moving silently in a straight line at very high speed. During the 3-4 second observation, the witness felt pressure and received an electric shock. The dog ran away towards the house, no longer responding to its owner's commands. The witness filed two statements with the police, one on the day of the observation and the other 10 days later. The details of the first statement, as well as those gathered at the scene, support the hypothesis of an electrical phenomenon because: - the luminous sphere was observed in the immediate vicinity of the intersection of two power lines and a transformer; - the electric sphere followed a path aligned with one of the power lines; - a sudden and brief voltage drop was observed by local residents at the time of the observation; - the witness felt pressure and an electric shock. A ball of light can be produced by the ionization of air and suspended molecules in the presence of an intense electric field (here, presumably resulting from a malfunction). (The glow of a neon tube works with a gas ionized by an electric field). This type of phenomenon, following power lines, has already been observed, particularly after a storm (see the video). The initial analysis in 1988 failed to provide an explanation because it relied on the witness's second statement, which described seeing several spheres and the phenomenon being located within the field and much further from the road and the power line crossing. Today, we prefer to consider the first statement made that same day, whereas the subsequent statement may have been influenced (even without the witness's knowledge) by the numerous contacts or requests the witness received from neighbors and the media. The subsequent discovery of cases of glows along power lines also strengthens this hypothesis. GEIPAN classifies the case as B: observation of an electrical and plasma phenomenon.

summary: Observation of the passage of a luminous phenomenon with a trail. Straight trajectory.
description: One person reported an old sighting from late December 1988 (the date of the event is given arbitrarily). This recent testimony (February 2011) of an old sighting from 1988 is not precise in terms of date (the witness does not specify the day or the exact time of the sighting). Any investigation is therefore impossible. Nevertheless, the characteristics described could correspond to the observation by numerous witnesses of the national event of December 21, 1988, of the atmospheric reentry of a piece of the Cosmos 1954 satellite's fuel tank (published on the GEIPAN website: NATIONAL (975) 21.12.1988). In the absence of a precise date allowing this connection, the event is classified as category C, meaning investigation is impossible.

summary: Multiple observations of the passage of luminous balls of varying intensity in the sky: atmospheric reentry of an upper stage of a rocket.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named NUKU HIVA (987) 1988, is one of a group of cases recently re-examined. On October 22, 1988, at approximately 3:30 a.m., several witnesses in French Polynesia observed the passage of very bright orbs, white or reddish-orange according to the accounts. This luminous phenomenon followed a straight trajectory across the sky, and no unusual noise was heard. Four witness statements were collected belatedly. The gendarmerie investigation also noted that that night, two crews from the airlines New Zealand and UTA reported observing phenomena, including long condensation trails off the Marquesas Islands. Several luminous orbs moving together in the sky with trails, glows of varying intensity, some with ogival shapes: all these elements are characteristic of the atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid with fragmentation or of a spacecraft. The "spacecraft" hypothesis prevailed because it was observed over a fairly long period (> 1 minute) and the angular movement in the sky was not very rapid. At the time, GEIPAN had less experience with testimonies of this type, and access to information to identify the original object was more difficult. Today it is possible to identify in the NORAD (North American Aerospace Defense Command) directories a list of objects or craft that made a reentry that day (there are several) and, thanks to the final orbits given by NORAD and the tracking tools, to find the one passing in the geometric conditions conforming to the observation and therefore to the origin of the observation. As indicated in the attached reconstruction, at approximately 1:45 PM UTC on October 22nd, or 4:15 AM local time (witnesses are not very precise, testifying between 2 and 5 weeks after the observation and indicating around 4:00 AM), the space object ne19597, the upper stage of the rocket used to launch the Raduga 22 satellite, passed close to the observation site under geometric conditions consistent with those observed, that is, from NW to SE, as described by T3 and T4, the two witnesses best positioned (closest) to understand the trajectory. Given his location, it is understandable that T2 primarily perceived only the W to E component of the trajectory. However, the trajectory corresponding to T1's observation does not match at all (error in the report?). Considering other eyewitness accounts, and also the indications (see flight reports) from the crews of two airliners who described the same phenomenon while flying near Nuku-Hiva (with the first one indicating a westward to eastward direction), we consider that T1's testimony cannot be used to refute the hypothesis. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: atmospheric reentry of an upper stage of a rocket.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry.
description: On October 20, 1988, between 6:45 p.m. and 7:00 p.m., two witnesses observed a bright blue, luminous sphere with a trail of yellow-orange sparks moving very quickly along a vertical trajectory. The observation was very brief (2 to 3 seconds) and silent. The witnesses' description suggests that the object was re-entering the atmosphere.

summary: Observation of a bright point that disappears at high speed
description: On October 19, 1988, at approximately 8:45 PM, a witness observing the sky saw a stationary glow that disappeared after moving at high speed following approximately 10 seconds. No sound was heard. No other information is available.

summary: Observation of a luminous ball moving back and forth at high speed.
description: On Thursday, October 13, 1988, at approximately 8:30 p.m., a witness observed a bright yellow ball, about the size of a car headlight, moving back and forth at high speed for about half an hour. No sound was detected. The witness's spouse also witnessed the phenomenon. No further information could be gathered.

summary: Observation of a laser projector in a hypermarket
description: On October 6, 1988, at approximately 9:30 PM, several witnesses observed three bluish light sources moving slowly across the sky above the region. Police officers called to the scene confirmed the phenomenon, which disappeared completely around 12:30 AM. The investigation initially focused unsuccessfully on a possible helicopter theft, ultimately concluding that a supermarket was testing laser projectors for an advertising campaign.

summary: Observation of a bright point moving in a zig-zag pattern.
description: On Thursday, September 22, 1988, at 3:15 a.m., a witness observed a bright point the size of a large star for ten minutes. This point moved in a zigzag pattern and left a fluorescent green trail. No further information was gathered about this phenomenon.

summary: Likely observation of atmospheric reentry
description: On September 7, 1988, at approximately 11:00 PM, a witness observed the very rapid passage of a luminous sphere followed by a white trail that appeared to sparkle. The phenomenon crossed the sky in a fraction of a second. The witness's description suggests that it was likely an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Long and successive observations of a very bright phenomenon in the sky: observations of the planet Mars.
description: This observation, formerly known as TRUN (61) 06.09.1988, is classified as a D case by SEPRA. It was recently re-examined (see the Investigation Notes document). Starting on September 6, 1988, several people observed the presence and movement of an unknown luminous phenomenon in the sky. The long, successive observations on September 7 and 8 took place between 10 PM and 11 PM. This case is consistent (four witnesses, several photographs), and the description of the observed UFO is precise. The sincerity and credibility of the witnesses have never been questioned. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (duration of observation, shape, size, color) with a well-known astronomical object: the planet Mars. Furthermore, Mars was visible along the axis indicated by the witnesses and was particularly bright at that time. It is not the visual perception of the witnesses that is the issue, but rather their interpretation of their observation based on their feelings (fatigue, fear, night driving). In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of weak strangeness is classified as UAP A, an observation linked to a misidentification of the planet Mars.

summary: Observation of a probable atmospheric reentry.
description: On November 5, 1989, a taxi driver observed a bright light flashing across the Paris sky for a few seconds. A round, luminous object followed by a greenish trail crossed the sky. No other accounts were recorded. The witness's description corresponds to the observation of a probable atmospheric reentry.

summary: Numerous witnesses have reported a plausible observation of atmospheric reentry.
description: On the night of September 4-5, 1988, at approximately 1:15 AM, numerous witnesses across several departments in central France, primarily in Burgundy, observed a bright, oval-shaped glow, described as yellow or white by the witnesses, with a large reddish trail that rapidly crossed the sky for a few seconds. The phenomenon was particularly significant in the Yonne department, where many witnesses were able to observe it. Depending on their location, witnesses heard the sound of four or five explosions, more or less loud, as the phenomenon disappeared. This explosion was especially well perceived in the Nièvre and Yonne departments, but the phenomenon was observed as far away as the Essonne department. The phenomenon was likely a large-scale atmospheric reentry.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry
description: On August 17, 1988, at approximately 10:30 PM, several witnesses briefly observed an orange ball in the sky followed by a bluish light. The accounts differ somewhat, particularly regarding the perceived speed. Although the object could also be mistaken for the moon, it was most likely an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Probable sighting of an ultralight aircraft
description: On August 11, 1988, a witness observed for about ten minutes the passage of a white object which he himself identified as probably being an ultralight aircraft.

summary: Nighttime observations of flashing white lights appearing to originate from an elongated shape moving at high altitude: sighting of an airplane.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This case, previously classified as D and named LES ROUSSES 11.08.1988, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. This concerns the observation of a UFO (Unidentified Flying Object) with intermittent flashes by two witnesses on August 11, 1988, at approximately 12:50 AM. Trainee soldiers, they were bivouacking at a place called the Bonnefoy chalet in the Risoux forest, in the commune of Morez (39). The witnesses were initially intrigued by the presence of white flashes in the night sky, then by the speed and unusual trajectory of the UFO, as well as the absence of any noise. The UFO, described as an elongated shape, disappeared from their sight, taking a descending trajectory and being hidden by the landscape. The Gendarmerie, alerted to the incident, collected no other testimonies about this phenomenon during its investigation. The points of strangeness noted by the witnesses during their observation can all be explained by simple confusion with an aircraft and its anti-collision lights, observed under specific conditions. The speed of the UAP, described as being greater than that of a Mirage F1 except for T1, is in reality particularly difficult, if not impossible, to assess at night, without any fixed reference points and without knowing the UAP's altitude, even for a witness claiming to be accustomed to seeing Mirages. The perception of noise is also highly dependent on other factors, unknown in this case, such as the distance separating the witnesses from the UAP, the ambient noise, the witnesses' own hearing perception, the sound level emitted by the UAP, and the wind strength and direction. The GEIPAN archives contain numerous confirmed cases (including radar evidence) of aircraft sightings without noise perception. Therefore, lacking precise information on these parameters, the absence of noise perception is not conclusive. T1 also claims that the lights were too intense to be those of an airplane. However, we are in a particular and unusual observation situation for the witnesses. Indeed, they are in a temporary nighttime observation situation, in a forest, far from any light pollution or stray lights, whereas they usually reside in urban areas. Moreover, having been outside for several hours, their night vision has had ample time to adapt to the environment, which is particularly dark. As a result, any bright light, even distant, will appear very intense to them. Another strange aspect for the witnesses, and in particular for T1, is the impression that the UFO is moving in a sinusoidal pattern. The fact that T2 states that the UFO was moving in a straight line and that the flight path was irregular, that it [this shape] was always rising and falling quite rapidly, gives us clues about what T1 perceived and about the nature of the UFO's actual movement. The rapid alternation of the anti-collision lights placed at distances from the aircraft and the impossibility at night of perceiving the aircraft's shape can, from a suitable viewing angle, create a perceptual illusion of rapid sinusoidal movement based solely on the lights, whereas the movement is, of course, rectilinear. This can be seen in videos available online. The final point of strangeness noted by the witnesses concerns the UFO's apparent stop, then its descent towards the ground. This is easily explained by a temporary gain in altitude by the aircraft as it moved along the observation axis, creating an effect of apparent immobility. Once the aircraft reached its altitude, the observation angle decreased again until the aircraft disappeared behind the trees. Furthermore, the bright brightness of the aircraft's anti-collision lights, visible from a great distance, accentuated the impression that it remained relatively close; consequently, this final phase of observation was interpreted by witnesses as a descent, when in reality it was a movement away. The likelihood of an aircraft at this location and time, aside from the compatibility with the observation as assessed above, is high. There are 5 airports within a 120 km radius of the location, 4 of which are international and one is military. An aircraft departing from one of these airports is not yet at cruising altitude and can therefore create the illusions described with its various lights and altitude changes. The consistency is poor. All useful angular data is missing (dimensions of the UFO, initial and final elevation above the horizon). The temporal data is imprecise, or even missing. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: observation of an aircraft.

summary: Observation of a very bright green glow rotating rapidly in an ellipse for approximately 15 minutes.
description: On August 9, 1988, at approximately 10:45 PM, a witness observed a very bright green glow that moved rapidly in an elliptical path. A second green glow also appeared suddenly and eventually merged with the first. No sound was heard, and this phenomenon was observed for about fifteen minutes. While there is no evidence to definitively confirm it, this phenomenon strongly suggests the effects of a laser projector.

summary: OBSERVATION OF A SILENTLY MOVING OBJECT
description: From the terrace of his holiday villa, a witness, accompanied by his family, reported seeing a luminous, elongated object moving very quickly and silently during the night of August 6-7, 1988. The object disappeared without a trace. No further information could be gathered to explain this phenomenon.

summary: Observing a cylindrical object through binoculars
description: On the evening of July 30-31, 1988, around 9:30 p.m., witnesses observed, through binoculars, an illuminated cylindrical object moving slowly towards the sun. It disappeared behind clouds. No further information could be gathered.

summary: Likely observation of atmospheric reentry.
description: On the evening of July 18, 1988, a witness briefly observed an intense light. A blue ball, the size of the full moon, crossed the sky at very high speed and without noise. It was probably an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observations of "acrobatics" or "ballets" of several luminous balls in the cloudy sky: probable observations of lasers or skytracers.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named WINGLES (62) 28.06.1988, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined (see the investigation report). On the night of June 28, 1988, a witness (T1) and his wife (T2) observed successive appearances of luminous orbs in the cloudy sky, beginning at 10:20 PM. These spheres move rapidly and silently in all directions, performing acrobatic maneuvers or ballets. A large, ogive-shaped object appears on the T1 radar. Four flashing white beams emerge from this grayish mass. Stationary for about thirty seconds, it suddenly disappears at 2:10 AM. Only two eyewitness accounts were collected. The description may have seemed strange during the initial analysis of the case in 1988. With the experience acquired by GEIPAN (the French National Center for Information and Experimentation on Explosive Orbit), there is little doubt today. The description is consistent with reflections in the sky from a set of spotlights used for advertising purposes. The upward beams from the spotlights are barely visible here; the witnesses primarily see the impacts on a screen of sky. The pattern formed by these impacts is typical of the scanning and rotation capabilities of the devices used: a circular or ogive shape, depending on the perspective created by the angle of observation. - Large-amplitude, back-and-forth movements, sometimes always following the same trajectory, sometimes performing various patterns, as well as stops. - Color and brightness of UFOs: a whitish light that does not dazzle. In the GEIPAN experiment, various configurations can be encountered: visibility of impacts alone, beams alone, or both at the same time. Weather conditions determine visibility and the distance of visibility, and this explains the random or even fleeting nature of the phenomena (the spotlights of a nearby nightclub may only rarely be visible while another elsewhere produces distant and frequent effects): - Here, the presence of low cloud cover is verified, which can create a screen in the sky. - It is also noted that witnesses observe the presence of partial beams, just below the UFOs, or beams that regularly switch on and off, also below the UFOs. We know that the 1980s saw a significant increase in the use of this type of projector, both in nightclubs and at various events (fairs, concerts). Since the observation occurred on a Tuesday evening, the nightclub hypothesis can be ruled out (except perhaps for testing purposes), suggesting a one-off event that may have taken place in Lens (within a few kilometers) or its surrounding area. Almost 30 years later, it is difficult to investigate the possibility of the event further. The presence of the source (projectors) cannot be definitively established, but given its potential existence, the very strong correlation between a visual appearance unlike anything else (see investigation report) and the consistent weather conditions are sufficient to establish the hypothesis as probable. Consequently, Geipan classifies the case as B: probable observation of lasers or skytracer e.

summary: Observation of a large green ball.
description: On the night of May 3-4, 1988, surveillance agents at a naval air base spotted a green ball in the sky following a straight trajectory. No further information about this phenomenon was gathered.

summary: Observation of a slowly moving ball
description: On April 21, 1988, at 4:54 a.m., a witness, barely awake from a sleep filled with bizarre dreams, reported seeing a very bright white ball. This ball moved slowly, changing color and decreasing in size. The police investigation revealed that the testimony could be given little credence.

summary: Observation of a very bright object, as big as a star.
description: Witnesses observed a circular object, the size of a star and very bright, during the night of April 13-14, 1988. This object expanded and then immediately returned to its original size. It gradually disappeared over the horizon. No other information is available to explain this phenomenon.

summary: OBSERVATION OF 2 BALLS ABOVE A RADIO TRANSMITTER
description: On March 22, 1988, at approximately 8:15 PM, a witness in his vehicle observed first one, then two large, pink, fluorescent spheres above a radio transmitter. His observation lasted between five and eight minutes. The investigation yielded no further information.

summary: Brief observation of a bright light, no noise
description: During the night of February 6-7, 1988, two motorists traveling on the same road but at different times observed a luminous phenomenon. A sphere emitted an intense white light and appeared to be moving. No sound was heard. No other information could be gathered about this phenomenon.

summary: Observation of a luminous green ball moving from east to west
description: On February 4, 1988, between 7:45 p.m. and 8:30 p.m., two witnesses observed a green ball moving slowly from east to west. No further information could be gathered.

summary: Observation of a helmet-shaped object, imposing and changing direction
description: On January 26, 1988, at 9:15 PM, a witness repeatedly observed a large object flying at low altitude, whose shape reminded him of a helmet with two wings. No sound was heard during the object's movements. A white light emanated from within, which then turned orange. The object disappeared, moving rapidly away. No further information has been gathered about this phenomenon, which remains unexplained.
